newsitem.title: UK: IPE June Brent closes up on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: IPE June Brent closes up on technical buying.

text.p: IPE June Brent closed 25 cents higher at $18.94 a barrel on Friday on the back of what traders said was a a flurry of last minute technical buying.
"It's a really inflated close for some reason. It was mostly last minute buying," one broker said.

"Nothing is really behind, it has been the pattern for the whole week. You get some people with some MOC (Market On Close) buying to do, the floor gets wind of it and there's no selling around." NYMEX's WTI contract closed 11 cents higher at $20.45. "This is all technical, I don't believe it's got to do with oil reasons for one minute," the broker said, echoing earlier setntiment from brokers who said they were a little bit skeptical about the gains June Brent has made recently.

In the late afternoon Brent shed all of its earlier gains to trade lower after NYMEX slipped, traders said. It was trading six cents down at $18.63 a barrel by 1501 GMT after NYMEX fell to as low as $20.18.
Earlier a trader said that he was cautious of the gains made by crude since Thursday, when June Brent closed a hefty 55 cents up at $18.69.
"I question the crude's move on the upside," the broker said.

"I am very cautious, it has not been confirmed by the gasoline...I need to see (NYMEX) gasoline confirmation, minimum a break above 62.90 (cents a gallon), probably confirmed by a break above 63.40 (cents a gallon), which is the high we made last week," the broker said.
NYMEX's June gasoline closed 0.35 cents higher at 62.85 cents a gallon.

Other brokers have said that Brent's rally on Thursday was mostly from talks of operational problems in the gasoline production units at two U.S. Gulf refineries. The two U.S. companies have declined to comment on the speculation.
Earlier on Friday IPE May gas oil closed $1.75 higher at $170.75 at tonne but some traders said the rise was largely due to pre-weekend position squaring mixed with some fundamentals.
June gas oil also closed unchanged at $167.50. The May contract had hit a high of $171.25 but also a low of $169.00.
Some traders have said the market was drawing strength from forecasts of colder weather in the Northeast United States for the weekend. - Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
